GRU4Rec’s strongest directly relevant evidence remains its ranking-loss follow-up: ordinary BPR/TOP1 gradients become diluted by easy negatives; BPR-max emphasizes high-scoring competitors through softmax weights and regularizes negative scores. The official implementation recommends BPR-max or cross-entropy and supports additional negatives plus sampling-probability correction for cross-entropy. These are established GRU-family alternatives, without requiring architecture replacement. [GRU4Rec paper](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf), [official implementation](https://github.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec).

Recent theory supports controlled hardness rather than always selecting the hardest item. A WWW 2023 paper connects hard-negative BPR to partial AUC, which better matches top-K objectives; suitable hardness depends on dataset and K. A 2024 sampled-softmax study identifies informative hard-negative gradients and ranking benefits, but also warns that similarity parameterization affects representation quality. Neither establishes gains for this Electronics split. [Hard-negative theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.03472), [sampled-softmax study](https://zlstwebsite.github.io/Zlst/publication/on-the-effectiveness-of-sampled-softmax-loss-for-item-recommendation/).

False negatives remain a concern: unobserved items can represent genuine interests, so aggressive mining can penalize plausible recommendations. UFNRec documents this issue; a 2024 sequential-recommendation comparison also finds sampling outcomes depend on dataset popularity structure. Practical hypothesis: compare BPR-max and sampled cross-entropy within the same GRU4Rec backbone, vary negative-pool size and hardness conservatively, and exclude training-observed positives from negatives. Preserve one independently trained model per category; choose using fixed four-category macro validation HR@10. Improved sampled margins alone do not establish generalization. [False-negative evidence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116), [sampling comparison](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276).
